reasons: No tests are visible in the packet.
Some views fall back to raw IDs or blank states when data is missing, and it is not clear whether users are warned in every case.
Several figures depend on how signals were classified, which this file does not check.

terms.meaning: a table where each cell's shade shows how many items it holds
the one solution a signal is mainly about
the event or cause that led to a signal
the shared rulebook of labels, definitions and rules used to classify signals
a priority level from 1 (pursue) to 4 (weak evidence)
capital spending, the money a project plans to spend to build or expand
an opportunity that is inferred rather than stated in a source
a value a parent passes into a component, like an argument to a function

sections.name: File setup, shortTrigger, Axis
sections.title: Imports, short trigger names and axis shape
sections.what: Brings in icons, data types, labels and helpers. The short trigger helper keeps only the text before the first comma and capitalises it, so long trigger names fit on screen.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps labels short in the grids and bars.
sections.watch_out: A trigger name that contains a comma will be cut at the comma.

sections.name: Heatmap
sections.title: Reusable count grid with totals
sections.what: Draws a table of counts with the rows and columns chosen by the caller. Shade grows with each cell's count, row and column totals appear, and clicking a cell reports its row and column. Empty cells show a dot and the note says they are research gaps, not missing opportunities.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared grid keeps the Analysis views looking and behaving the same.
sections.watch_out: Shading is relative to the largest cell in the current grid, so colours do not match between two different views.

sections.name: solutionAxis, solutionOf
sections.title: Solution rows and the unclassified row
sections.what: Lists only the solutions that have at least one signal in the current view, and counts how many solutions were hidden. Signals with no primary solution go into a row called Not yet classified.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps empty solutions off the chart so it stays readable.
sections.watch_out: The solution label drops the text 'CPA-' from the ID, so a solution ID with a different prefix will show differently.

sections.name: SolutionPriority
sections.title: Solution by priority tier grid
sections.what: Shows how many signals for each solution sit in each priority tier, from Tier 1 (pursue) to Tier 4 (weak evidence). Clicking a cell reports the solution and tier to the parent.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows where the strongest signals sit across solutions.
sections.watch_out: Only the primary solution is counted, so a signal that fits two solutions appears under one only.

sections.name: SolutionTrigger
sections.title: Solution by trigger grid
sections.what: Shows which triggers lead to which solutions. Trigger columns come from the codebook plus any trigger found on the signals, and their labels come from the codebook when available.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Trigger columns are built from the signals present, so the table changes as the data changes.

sections.name: IndustryTheme, Bar
sections.title: Industry by theme grid and bar shape
sections.what: Shows industries as rows and the twelve most common research themes as columns, with a note on how many themes are shown out of the total. The bar shape defines one bar: its key, label, count and an optional emphasis.
sections.why: Likely reason: limiting to twelve themes keeps the grid readable.
sections.watch_out: Themes outside the top twelve are hidden from this view entirely.

sections.name: bars
sections.title: Shared bar chart builder
sections.what: Draws horizontal bars with a label, a count, and an optional share of the total. Prioritised bars get an up chevron and deprioritised bars a down chevron. Clicking a bar asks the parent to filter by it. Part of the fill styling line is cut off in the packet.
sections.why: Likely reason: one bar component keeps all bar lists consistent.
sections.watch_out: Special styling for the general-market and unmapped keys depends on exact key values, so changing those values loses the styling.

sections.name: Categories
sections.title: Solution and trigger rankings
sections.what: Builds two ranked bar lists: solutions by the number of signals with that primary solution, and triggers by the number of signals in each trigger family. Each carries the emphasis set in the codebook.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick ranking to read next to the grids.
sections.watch_out: Solutions with no signals are removed from the ranking, but the list depends on how signals were classified.

sections.name: CapexView
sections.title: Capex bands and largest sourced projects
sections.what: Counts signals in each capex band (mega, large, mid, small, plan, unknown) as bars. Lists up to eight of the largest sourced capex figures, ranked by their lower bound and excluding company-wide plans. Notes explain that only source-quoted amounts count, that unknown is not zero, and how many signals are still queued.
sections.why: Likely reason: the notes stop a missing figure from being read as zero.
sections.watch_out: Ranking uses the lower bound only, so a project with a higher upper estimate can still rank lower.

sections.name: Customise
sections.title: Links into the codebook editor
sections.what: Shows a short label and one button for each codebook section that defines a view's rows and columns. Each button opens the editor on that section. Hover text warns that saving re-classifies all signals.
sections.why: Stated in the code: it opens the editor on the sections that define a view's rows and columns.
sections.watch_out: Saving from the editor re-classifies every signal, which can change all the views at once.

sections.name: CompanyMix
sections.title: Client mix summary, strip and bars
sections.what: Works out how signals split between tracked clients and the general market. Shows the leading client (noting ties), the general-market share, how many clients have signals, a proportional strip, a bar list by client, and the top twenty companies named in general-market signals. Clicking a client sets the client filter.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows whose signals dominate the feed.
sections.watch_out: A signal naming two clients counts toward both, so client shares can add up to more than 100 percent.

sections.name: SignalTypes
sections.title: Signal types, new-project test and nature
sections.what: Shows signal types from the codebook as bars, plus any unknown types found in the data and a Not yet classified bar. Shows counts for new-project yes, does not count, and pending, and bars by nature (problem, opportunity, whitespace). The yes count opens the announcements view.
sections.why: Stated in the code: the new-project test is kept separate from signal type and nature.
sections.watch_out: Does not count is calculated by subtraction, so any signal with a new-project record whose status is not yes is counted there, even when its assessment is incomplete.

summary: Builds the Analysis view of the Opportunity Map: count grids and bar charts that break signals down by solution, trigger, industry, theme, capex, client and signal type.
purpose: Helps a user spot patterns across signals and click any cell or bar to filter the feed and map.
why: Likely reason: each view answers a different question about the same signals. Blank cells are kept as research gaps because a missing signal is not the same as no opportunity.
how: 1. Receives the signal list, the codebook, and the current selections. 2. Each view counts signals along two chosen axes or along one axis. 3. Draws a shaded grid or a bar list with totals. 4. A click passes the chosen row, column or value back to the parent, which filters the feed.
inputs: Lists of signals, solutions and triggers, the codebook, a lookup for industry names, tracked client accounts, the current client and company selections, and click callbacks.
outputs: Tables, bars and summary figures on screen, and click events passed to the parent.
risks: Client shares can add up to more than 100 percent when a signal names two clients. Capex figures are only as good as their sources. Shading is relative to each grid, so colours do not compare across views. Some views hide zero-count rows.
debug: If a count looks wrong, check the signal's mapping fields, since the views read primary solution and trigger family directly. If a view is empty, check whether the filtered signal list is empty. If a label shows a raw ID, check whether that ID exists in the codebook.
